em_1_minuto.titulo: Can we help bone rebuild itself?
em_1_minuto.texto: In tissue engineering, cells need a support, a “scaffold”, to grow and form new tissue. The study tested a scaffold made of three natural materials.
In the lab, cells that will become osteoblasts (the cells that make bone) were grown on the scaffold and compared with cells grown directly on the plate.
The cells thrived on the scaffold, deposited more mineral nodules in 14 days and switched on bone-forming genes earlier.
The scaffold may be useful in future treatments to regenerate bone. These are still lab results.

secoes.titulo: What a scaffold is, and why these materials
secoes.lede: To regenerate a tissue, cells need a place to attach, grow and work.

blocos.html:
In tissue engineering, a scaffold is a three-dimensional structure that supports cells, like scaffolding on a building site. A good scaffold must be well tolerated by the body, have pores for cells to enter and, ideally, stimulate the formation of the desired tissue.

The scaffold in this study is lamellar and dense, that is, made of compact layers, and combines three materials of natural origin.

itens.texto: Obtained from chitin, found in crustacean shells. It is biocompatible and biodegradable, widely used in biomaterials.
The main protein in the organic part of bone. It serves as the base where minerals are deposited.
A molecule naturally present in tissues. It holds water and takes part in communication between cells.

secoes.lede: An in vitro study, that is, with cells in the lab.

itens.texto: Immortalized pre-osteoblastic cells were used: cells that will still turn into osteoblasts, the ones responsible for making bone.
Control: cells grown directly on the plastic plate. Scaffold: cells grown on the chitosan, type I collagen and hyaluronic acid scaffold.
Each group was grown in standard medium and in osteogenic medium, which contains substances that stimulate bone formation.
The cells' metabolic activity (whether they were healthy), the deposit of mineral nodules, the activity of the enzyme alkaline phosphatase and the activation of the Runx2 and Ocn genes.

secoes.titulo: The scaffold pushed the cells toward becoming bone
secoes.lede: Signs of bone formation appeared stronger and sooner in the cells on the scaffold.

itens.texto: The metabolic activity of cells on the scaffold was similar to the control: the material did not harm the cells.
After 14 days, there were more mineral nodules deposited on the scaffold than in the control, in both standard and osteogenic media.
The scaffold itself increased the activity of this enzyme, which paves the way for bone mineralization.
mRNA production from the Runx2 and Ocn genes increased, and earlier than in the control group.

itens: Pre-osteoblast: the cell doesn't make bone yet

secoes.titulo: What the study allows us to say
secoes.lede: An early lab step toward new materials for regenerating bone.

blocos.html:
The dense lamellar scaffold of chitosan, type I collagen and hyaluronic acid stimulated the cells to mature toward bone. The authors conclude that it is a promising material for future bone regeneration strategies.

Since this is a lab study with cells, tests in animals and then in people are still needed.

glossario.def: 3D structure that supports cells so they can grow and form a tissue.
Field that combines cells, materials and chemical signals to rebuild body tissues.
Natural polymer obtained from the chitin in crustacean shells. Biocompatible and biodegradable.
The most abundant protein in bone, skin and tendons.
Natural tissue molecule that holds water and helps cells communicate.
Cell that produces the bone matrix.
Still-immature cell that can turn into an osteoblast.
Culture medium with substances that stimulate cells to form bone.
Spots where cells deposit calcium and phosphate, the beginning of the hard part of bone.
Enzyme produced by osteoblasts that helps mineralize bone.
Marker genes of bone formation: Runx2 starts the process and osteocalcin marks the mature osteoblast.
The “working copy” of a gene. More mRNA means the gene is more active.
